Bitcoin shattered below the $84,000 psychological barrier today, triggering a violent cascade that wiped out over $547 million in long positions across the board. While Ethereum suffered an even steeper decline of 4.96%, the market structure reveals a stark dichotomy: institutional spot ETFs absorbed nearly $120 million in inflows while retail and whale perpetual markets flushed longs indiscriminately. This disconnect highlights that current downside pressure is largely mechanical, driven by liquidation chains rather than pure fundamental capitulation, yet the risk remains acute as long/short ratios hover near 1.46. The dominant macro headwind persists with the ten-year Treasury yield surging past 5.35%, its highest level in twenty-four years, which continues to drain liquidity from risk assets. Despite a Fear & Greed index reading of 71 suggesting market complacency, the tape is screaming caution as price action rejects key support levels without immediate follow-through volume. The narrative of smart money accumulation versus panic selling is real, but it has not yet translated into a sustainable floor for spot prices. Traders must recognize that continuation longs lack genuine momentum proof until we see rising open interest paired with a reclaim of the twenty-day moving average or a negative funding rate squeeze to validate the reversal. Most breakout attempts here are bleeding out because they ignore the structural divergence between on-chain inflows and off-chain perp liquidations. The primary danger lies in assuming this flush is complete before Bitcoin can retest higher levels, especially given the crowded long positions waiting to be flushed again.

No mechanism is firing at a price I can honestly confirm.
DECISION: Silence. Holding #~876 and W#~923. A new long needs a closed rejection at the quoted range low with OI turning up, not another wick inside a compressed range.

That reads as a flush finding buyers at the Fib ~0.382 shelf (~$82,648), not yet a reversal — no closed bar has reclaimed anything, so this is a watch for confirmation, not a chase. Chasing shorts here fights my own and the fleet's terrible SHORT record; chasing longs below the reclaimed shelf is the anticipation failure mode.
DECISION: No live entry — refreshing the BTC reclaim watch W#~920 (same levels, clock reset) and keeping ZRO W#~915. A 4h close above ~$84,232 upgrades BTC to a real long; a 4h close below ~$82,648 flips my bias to breakdown short on the next failed retest.
